sourceInformation.source: Beauty and the Beast (Imagic, Intellivision, 1982), designed by Wendell Brown
sourceInformation.perspective: Fixed side view; x/z gameplay with projected dimensional pixel art
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge 0.89.1 (one Renderer.ppu correction), JavaScript, Canvas 2D, Web Audio; AI Hub protocol 1 / pristine client 1.4.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original shaded procedural pixel art, layered masonry, toy-like facade, warm windows and a teal evening skyline
sourceInformation.animation: Native Humanoid rigs and continuous pose blending; native creature animation; procedural shutters, boulders and biplane
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-generated chip music, synthesized effects and gibberish character barks. Music defaults to 10%.
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 players in AI Hub shared-world sessions, authoritative host including a non-playing server; standalone solo and local co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Node semantic scenarios and uncheated full solo/co-op routes; packaged Chromium/WebKit/Firefox, emulated controllers and CDP-injected multi-contact touch; actual audio analyser/offline synthesis; Hub harness and full normal/degraded/server-host rescue routes. Physical devices, human first-run pacing and subjective listening: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Original Imagic manual, INTV Funhouse illustrated archive and six sampled gameplay-video frames; full engine API/asset guide/platformer kit and AI Hub README/shared-world example. Exact source melody/synthesis and human audio audition: unknown.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux, Ubuntu 26.04 on WSL2

testingFeedback: 29 confirmed defects fixed, plus 2 preventive integration findings clarified during review. The ledger records all 31 in artifacts/defects.json. Test-driver mistakes are excluded.

2 confirmed critical issues: malformed-checkpoint null-ledger handling and standalone audio remaining stopped on start/retry. The Hub namespace/schema findings were preventive contract clarifications already mitigated by integrated aliases, not observed runtime failures.

The uncheated full-route tests: they required all window climbs, jumps, every hazard family, powered clears, recovery, all three pursuits, rescue and the complete plane departure. Separate shared-world browser rescue tests verify the same ending and authoritative ledger across copies.

The original attract-exit assertion inspected the previous run’s cumulative jumps. An unsynchronized browser-clock fixture also injected unintended network delay. These test-driver failures were corrected with held-input checks and explicit shared-clock/delivery-delay bounds; they are excluded from the game defect count.
engineFeedback: The native Platformer controller, shaded Humanoid rigs, pixel material/render helpers and complete settings/menu foundation made a coherent base.

Yes. Renderer.ppu multiplied camera zoom twice; native actor scratch bounds clipped long plane banners. Snapshot construction also needed explicit restoration of native private timing state. Packaged audio testing exposed a start/resume integration mistake.
The authoritative reversible shutter traversal, authored encounter scheduler, shared scoring/checkpoints and co-op snapshot/input transport.
Keeping reversible window actions, native body state, character grip poses, snapshot restoration and remote interpolation consistent.
One line in the full engine: Renderer.ppu now returns view.scale because Game._applyView already includes zoom. Six projection-scale checks cover the correction. The Hub client is unchanged.
Add a documented serializable, reversible traversal action for Platformer bodies, including an example of generic E.Action use and snapshot restoration.
promptFeedback: The clear creative mandate, distinctive window/heart mechanics, native-style direction and explicit complete-rescue acceptance tests.

The SOURCE field includes the release year, while the filename uses a SOURCE placeholder without a slug convention. The final basename retains 1982. Repeated acceptance requirements also made the plan longer than necessary.
Integrating native traversal and animation, input parity, a complete comic ending and authoritative co-op into one offline HTML, then verifying the actual package.
Keep the concrete acceptance tests and delivery schema, but consolidate repeated rationale and add a small reference harness for the required input/lifecycle contracts.

aiHub.name: Beauty and the Tall Tale
aiHub.tagline: Small hero. Big bully. Very tall building.
aiHub.description: Climb the shuttered windows of the Mutton Building, dodge Hank’s boulders and catch Mabel’s hearts for a six-second rampage. Rescue her on the rooftop and catch a biplane home, solo or together.
aiHub.controls: WASD/arrows or stick/d-pad: move and climb; Space/Cross: jump; Escape/Options: menu; touch: left thumb move/climb, right tap jump.
